shapes.name: array_length
shapes.reason: An array's own length, not a caller-supplied number. A JS array cannot be longer than the safe-integer range, so the read has nothing to saturate; the budget on that length is the array-length guard's, which the shared wasmArrayLikeLength applies.

shapes.name: array_element
shapes.reason: An element read from an array whose length was taken first, indexed by the loop counter. The value is a caller-supplied number like any other, but the receiver is the element rather than a named option, so it carries no field name a range error could report; the element's own domain is checked where the struct it fills is validated.

narrowings.reason: An enum ordinal range-checked against the warp-mode bounds before the cast is used, so a saturated value is refused by name.

readers.reason: Not a conversion: the narrowing is delegated whole to the shared intProperty, and what is local is the field's own domain. The shared reader guarantees the value survived the conversion unchanged, which a negative frame count does, and nothing downstream asks whether one means anything -- the peak picker returned an ordinary onset list for -1. The six onset window fields are the only place that domain applies, so asking it at the field keeps it off every other integer option.

A default seeder rather than an options-bag reader: it rejects a non-number, turns a non-positive value into a deterministic seed, and refuses anything past the type's maximum by name. Every value in the type's range is a legal seed, so truncating a fractional one cannot land outside the domain -- driving it, a seed moves the synthesized response, 4294967296 and Infinity are refused, and 0 / -1 / NaN all fall back to the documented default.

Delegates its narrowing to the shared checkedFloatFromVal rather than casting, so the conversion contract is single-sourced and only the default-and-absence handling is local. Kept out of the shared header for the same reason as its integer sibling: its options bag is positional in a way the generic reader is not. Not the same defect as the integer one and it had to be measured separately -- an overflow here produces inf rather than a plausible in-domain number, and the config validator refuses NaN but accepted inf, so four distinct absurd requests reached one identical result.

Delegates its narrowing to the shared checkedIntFromVal rather than casting, so the conversion contract is single-sourced and only the default-and-absence handling is local. Kept out of the shared header because its options bag is positional in a way the generic reader is not.

An enum resolver for the pan-law ordinal, taking the string and numeric spellings together. The numeric path requires a finite, integral value inside the enum's bounds before the cast, so a saturated, negative, fractional or non-finite ordinal is refused by name; the two legal ordinals pan differently, which is what makes those refusals a measurement rather than an unread field.

Reads through double rather than narrowing, so no integer cast happens here and the inline-narrowing population does not see it. It is a second numeric reader outside the shared family all the same. Its own range check is the mechanism: a value outside [0, max] or a fractional one is refused naming the field, and a non-finite one is refused by the shared requireNumberProperty it reads through.

The floating-point sibling of integerField, under the same standing. It type-checks and refuses a non-finite value through the shared requireNumberProperty and returns the double unnarrowed; the float narrowing is the caller's, and it can only overflow for values already far outside the field's physical domain, where the representable neighbours render identically.

An enum resolver for the sample loop mode, accepting the SoundFont numeric value and the name spellings. The numeric path is integerField's, so the ordinal is refused outside [0, 3] and for a fractional or non-finite value; an unknown name is refused naming the accepted set.

An enum resolver, not a size reader: the ordinal it returns is range-checked by the C ABI against the curve enum's bounds. Recorded here rather than folded into the shared family because the reader shape is incidental -- it exists to accept both the string and the numeric spelling of one enum.

The sibling enum resolver for the automation target kind. Like automationCurveFromVal it exists to accept both spellings of one enum, and its numeric path requires a finite, integral ordinal inside the enum's bounds before the cast, so a saturated, negative or fractional one is refused rather than landing on a member.
